Seasons are a thing I do not understand. I know when the days grow shorter and the nights longer, and when the air turns cold and the leaves fall. I know when to hunt, when to rest, and when to call. Weather is a thing I know by the feel of the air, the sound of the wind, the way the leaves tremble. I do not know how to write it, but I know the sound of it, and sometimes I hear it in the wind or the call of the night. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Boiling is a word I have heard, but not the meaning. The stream is always cold. The stream is where I bathe, and I do not know what it is to boil.
